questions.q: How can an analyst recognize a custom field, per this lesson?
options: By the __c suffix on its API name
Custom fields are always colored red in the Salesforce UI
Custom fields can only ever be Picklist type
They always have the word 'Custom' in their label
questions.explain: Just like custom objects, every custom field carries a __c suffix on its API name.

questions.q: Why can't an analyst assume a custom field like Renewal_Risk_Score__c means the same thing in every org, per this lesson?
options: Custom fields are built to model what's unique to a specific org's business, so their type and values can differ completely between orgs
Custom fields are randomly generated and have no consistent meaning even within one org
Renewal_Risk_Score__c is actually a standard Salesforce field
Custom fields cannot hold different values across records
questions.explain: The lesson explains this field might be a manually entered picklist in one org and an automatically calculated formula in another.

questions.q: Per the lesson's four-question checklist, what should an analyst check about a custom field's object, drawing on Lesson 18?
options: Whether the object has Record Types, since the field's relevance or valid values may differ by Record Type
Whether the object is a standard object
Whether the object has ever been renamed
Whether the object has more than 100 fields total
questions.explain: The checklist explicitly ties back to Record Types from Lesson 18, since a field's meaning can vary by Record Type.

questions.q: Per the checklist, why should an analyst check whether a custom field is on the Page Layout being compared against, drawing on Lesson 19?
options: Because a business user not recognizing the field doesn't mean the field or the report is wrong
Because fields not on a Page Layout cannot appear in reports
Because Page Layouts determine a field's data type
Because Page Layouts are unrelated to custom fields
questions.explain: This directly reuses the Lesson 19 point: a Page Layout only controls visibility, not whether the field genuinely holds data.

questions.q: What is the practical takeaway of this lesson for an analyst moving between Salesforce orgs?
options: Never carry an assumption about a custom field's meaning, values, or existence from one org into another
All custom fields across all orgs share identical meanings and values
Custom fields should never be used in any report
Only Salesforce admins are permitted to view custom field data
questions.explain: The lesson's core guidance is that custom fields, unlike standard fields, carry no guarantee of consistent meaning across orgs.
